figures.label: Figure 1
figures.legend: Study pipeline. RR intervals derived from ambulatory ECG beat annotations are cut into 60-beat windows and scored by a window-level AF detector. The patient-adaptive hidden Markov quantifier (PA-HMMQ) treats the patient's window sequence as a two-state Markov chain whose rhythm dynamics are re-estimated for each patient (maximum-a-posteriori expectation–maximisation with a prior centred on source dynamics from calibration patients A), and returns the posterior expected burden. Posterior sampling gives a model-based standard deviation that is converted into a 90% conformal interval using calibration patients B. External cohorts are never used for training or calibration.
figures.alt: Flow diagram with five boxes in a row: ambulatory ECG beat annotations to RR intervals, 60-beat windows, window detector producing AF probability, patient-adaptive HMM quantifier, and burden with 90% conformal interval. Three boxes below feed into the last three: calibration patients A, posterior sampling, calibration patients B.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.legend: Per-patient AF-burden mean absolute error (percentage points) of nine estimators and the pre-registered PA-HMMQ variant in the development test set and three external cohorts, LightGBM detector. Points, mean over five seeds; bars, ±1 SD. Blue, PA-HMMQ variants. Abbreviations as in Table 2.
figures.alt: Four dot-plot panels, one per cohort, listing ten burden estimators on the vertical axis and mean absolute error on the horizontal axis; the final PA-HMMQ has the lowest error in every panel.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.legend: Bland–Altman plots of estimated versus reference AF burden in the pooled external cohorts for classify-and-count (left) and the final PA-HMMQ (right), LightGBM detector, estimates averaged over seeds. Hollow markers: patients with any reference atrial flutter. Solid line, mean difference; dashed lines, 95% limits of agreement. The diagonal band of points with large positive differences consists mainly of Icentia11k patients labelled atrial flutter, whose irregular ventricular response is classified as AF.
figures.alt: Two scatter plots of difference against mean burden. Most points lie on zero; a diagonal line of hollow points with large positive differences corresponds to flutter patients; the right panel shows a slightly smaller bias.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.legend: Empirical coverage (left) and mean width (right, log scale) of 90% per-patient burden intervals by method and cohort, LightGBM detector (mean ± SD over seeds). Dashed line, nominal coverage 0.90.
figures.alt: Two dot-plot panels. Left: coverage of seven interval methods in four cohorts relative to a dashed 0.90 line. Right: mean interval width on a logarithmic axis, smallest for normalised conformal intervals of the final PA-HMMQ.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.legend: Robustness of burden estimators in SHDB-AF to simulated missed and false R peaks, R-peak timing jitter and premature beats with compensatory pauses, for the LightGBM (left) and RRNet (right) detectors. Mean absolute error ± SD over seeds.
figures.alt: Two line charts of mean absolute error across nine perturbation conditions for five estimators; errors rise with false R peaks and ectopy, and the final PA-HMMQ remains lowest or close to lowest in most conditions.

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.legend: Mean absolute error by reference burden stratum in the pooled external cohorts (LightGBM detector; logarithmic axis). Strata: AF-free (0%), >0–1%, >1–10%, >10–50% and >50% burden.
figures.alt: Line chart with five burden strata on the horizontal axis and error on a logarithmic vertical axis for four estimators; errors are largest in intermediate strata.
